method: Headless Chromium 142 driven by Playwright in a Linux container on Modal; the page is served off disk by request interception because the local sandbox forbids binding a socket. Frame times are read from the scene's own rAF timestamps over a 12 s run after a warm-up. Every shader program is asserted to have linked before the frame rate is trusted, because a program that fails to compile silently removes its work from the frame budget.
why_not_the_user_laptop: Google Chrome, Playwright Chromium and Playwright WebKit all abort with SIGABRT when launched inside this agent sandbox, so no browser could be run on the user's machine. tools/benchmark_heart3d.py runs unchanged on a normal macOS shell: `python tools/benchmark_heart3d.py --engine chrome --seconds 12`.

hardware_accelerated.renderer: ANGLE (NVIDIA Corporation, NVIDIA A10/PCIe/SSE2, OpenGL ES 3.2)

vsync_note: 16.7 ms median with a 16.7 ms p95 is the 60 Hz presentation interval: the scene is vsync-limited, not GPU-limited, so 60 fps is a floor on this hardware rather than a ceiling measurement.
